# ADR-001: hello, world

## Context
A hello-world page, as a NAVI demo. Must work offline, must look like it belongs to NAVI.

## Decision
One HTML file, no dependencies, no network calls. The NAVI block logo decodes out of static, then the greeting,
then the line the user wrote: “{{line}}”. System monospace font only. Hard size budget: 12 KB.

## Consequences
- Nothing to install, nothing to fetch, nothing to leak (ADVERSARY C1).
- The 12 KB cap keeps it honest (LEDGER C2). Measured: 6.7 KB.
- No web fonts means the exact glyph shapes vary by machine. Accepted.

## Rejected
- A web font for the greeting: phones home. Rejected.
- A framework: for one page. Rejected without discussion.

## Accepted risks
- The glitch effect uses CSS animations: on a very old browser it degrades to plain text.

events.subject: PROPOSAL-1: a single index.html, nothing else
events.body:
- One file: HTML + CSS + a little JS. No build step, no framework, no CDN.
- The NAVI block logo decodes out of static (like the boot screen), then "hello, world" with the RGB-split glitch.
- Six sagging power lines on a canvas, scanlines on top, the hub rings idling under the greeting.
- A closing line under the greeting, typed out character by character.
- Fonts: whatever monospace the machine has. Colours: the wired palette.
- Why: a hello world should be readable in full in one sitting, by a human.

events.subject: C1: "whatever font" can become a web font
events.body: The proposal says no CDN, then says "fonts: whatever". A @font-face to Google Fonts would phone home on every visit and leak the visitor's IP. Fix: system monospace only, stated as a hard rule in the file. Confirm no external URL of any kind.
a hello world has no excuse to be heavy. put a number on it.

events.subject: C2: no size budget
events.body: Canvas + glitch + typing + logo is fine, but "a little JS" is not a number. Cap the whole file at 12 KB and measure it before you call it done. Over budget means something is doing work the page does not need.

- Everything else unchanged.
One thing the council can't decide for you: what should the page say? Write the line that types out under “hello, world”.
